oneLiner: 光在同种均匀介质中沿直线传播，形成影与小孔成像。
oneLinerEn: Light travels in straight lines in uniform media, forming shadows and pinhole images.
detail: 光在同种均匀介质中沿直线传播，影子、小孔成像、日食与月食都由它而来。条件有两条，同种且均匀，缺任何一条光都可能拐弯：大气密度随高度连续变化，星光穿过大气会被连续折射，太阳实际还在地平线下约 0.5° 时就已经能被看见，海市蜃楼同样是密度梯度造的弯（详见折射一条）。小孔成像是这条最干净的证据——孔足够小时屏上出现倒立的像，像的大小与屏到孔的距离成正比，把屏推远就放大像；孔太大时一个物点会摊成一片投影区，像反而糊成光斑，而孔极小时衍射又把它抹开，所以「小孔」其实存在一个中间最优值。墨家《墨经》在公元前四五世纪就记下小孔成像的「景倒」，是现存最早的光学实验记录之一。影子还分本影（完全照不到）与半影（只被部分遮住），日食的类型正由观察者落在哪个影区决定：本影扫过的窄带是日全食，本影延长线（伪本影）带上是日环食，半影区只看到日偏食；月食是月亮走进地球的本影，一次可同时被半个夜半球看到，所以「此地日全食、彼地看不见」并不矛盾。工程上也把直线传播当尺子用：激光准直给隧道掘进与砌墙导向，射击的「缺口—准星—目标」三点一线、排队看齐、用杆影相似三角形测楼高与井深。真空中的光速 c≈3.00×10⁸ m/s，是宇宙速度上限；空气中几乎不变（n≈1.0003，约 29.99 万公里每秒），水中约 2.26 万公里每秒，玻璃中约 20 万公里每秒。光年就是这一速度走一年的距离，约 9.46×10¹⁵ m，是长度单位而不是时间单位。最后提醒：严格说没有一条光线绝对直，衍射总会在影子边缘留下条纹，只是在宏观尺度上偏离小到可以忽略——「直线传播」是几何光学的第一条近似，而不是光的本性。
detailEn: Light travels in straight lines within a single uniform medium, and shadows, pinhole images, solar and lunar eclipses all follow from this. Two conditions are bundled here—same medium, and uniform—and if either fails light can bend: air density changes continuously with height, starlight is refracted all the way down, so the Sun is already visible when it is still some 0.5° below the horizon, and mirages are the same gradient trick (see the refraction entry). A pinhole camera is the cleanest evidence: with a small enough hole the screen shows an inverted image whose size grows in proportion to screen distance, so pushing the screen back magnifies it; open the hole too wide and each object point smears into a patch, while a tiny hole lets diffraction blur it again—there really is an optimum hole size. The Mohist Canon of the 5th–4th centuries BCE recorded the inverted image of a pinhole, among the earliest optics experiments on record. A shadow has two zones, the umbra where light is wholly blocked and the penumbra where it is partly blocked, and which zone an observer stands in decides the eclipse type: a narrow track of umbra gives a total solar eclipse, the extension of the cone (antumbra) gives an annular one, and the penumbra only shows a partial eclipse; a lunar eclipse is the Moon entering Earth's umbra and is visible to the whole night hemisphere at once, so 'total here, invisible there' is not a contradiction. Straight-line propagation is also used as a ruler: laser alignment guides tunnel boring and wall laying, 'notch, bead and target in one line' governs rifle aiming, queues line up by the same logic, and shadow similar-triangles measure building heights and well depths. The vacuum speed of light c≈3.00×10⁸ m/s is the cosmic limit; in air it barely changes (n≈1.0003, about 299,900 km/s), in water it is roughly 226,000 km/s and in glass 200,000 km/s. A light-year is the distance covered at that speed in one year, about 9.46×10¹⁵ m—a unit of length, never of time. One caveat: no ray is ever perfectly straight, diffraction always fringes a shadow edge, and 'rectilinear propagation' is the first approximation of geometric optics rather than the nature of light.

oneLiner: 反射角等于入射角；分镜面反射与漫反射。
oneLinerEn: Angle of reflection equals angle of incidence; specular or diffuse.
detail: 反射定律只有三句：反射光线与入射光线、法线在同一平面内，分居法线两侧，反射角等于入射角。这里的角一律是对法线量的而不是对镜面量的——说「光线与镜面成 30°」时入射角其实是 60°，这是本条最高频的错误。镜面自己转过 θ，反射线会转过 2θ，因为入射角本身就变了 θ；光路可逆，逆着反射线打回去必沿原路出射，解题与角反射器都靠这一句。反射分两类：平静水面与抛光金属是镜面反射，平行束被整束按同一方向弹回，所以只在特定角度刺眼；纸、墙、布与粉笔字是漫反射，微观上每一点都严格守反射定律，只是各点法线方向杂乱，把光散向四面八方——正因如此我们从任何角度都看得见本身不发光的物体，而「漫反射不遵守反射定律」是彻底的错话。黑板某处反光看不清字，就是那一片被磨得太光滑而起镜面反射，办法是磨砂或涂白，不是擦得更亮；投影幕与电影幕用粗糙白布，一为漫向全场，二为不改变颜色（见「物体的颜色」条）。两面平面镜夹角为 θ 时成 360/θ−1 个像（θ=90° 得 3 个、60° 得 5 个），万花筒正是靠它把碎片复制成对称图案。相互垂直的两面镜有个极有用的性质：出射线总与入射线平行而方向相反；三块两两垂直的镜面组成的角反射器更进一步——无论光从哪个方向来都被沿原路送回。自行车尾灯、道路标志与反光服里的微棱镜膜、卫星上的角反射器阵列都是它，阿波罗计划留在月面的反射器至今用于激光测距；雷达与声呐也挂角反射器让目标在屏幕上更醒目。潜望镜与光路转向可用平面镜，也可用全反射棱镜（后者不依赖镀层、更耐久，见「全反射」条）。最后一条常与偏振连着：自然光以约 56°（玻璃的布鲁斯特角）掠射时，反射的那部分是部分偏振光，这就是偏振太阳镜能压掉路面与水面反光的根据（见「偏振」条）。
detailEn: The law of reflection has just three clauses: the reflected ray, the incident ray and the normal lie in one plane; the first two sit on opposite sides of it; and the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. Every angle here is measured from the normal, never from the surface—say 'the ray makes 30° with the mirror' and the incidence angle is really 60°, the single most common slip in this topic. Rotate the mirror itself by θ and the reflected ray swings by 2θ, because the incidence angle changed by θ on its own. Light paths are reversible: send a ray back along the reflected direction and it exits along the original one, a fact used both in problem-solving and in corner reflectors. Reflection comes in two kinds. Still water and polished metal give specular reflection, sending a parallel bundle off in one direction, which is why it dazzles only from particular angles. Paper, walls, cloth and chalk letters give diffuse reflection: microscopically every point obeys the law exactly, but their normals point every which way, so light is scattered into all directions. That scattering is precisely why we can see non-luminous objects from anywhere, and 'diffuse reflection breaks the law' is simply wrong. When a glare patch on a blackboard hides the writing, that spot has been polished smooth into specular reflection; the fix is to roughen or whiten it, not to wipe it shinier. Projection and cinema screens are coarse white cloth both to scatter light across the room and to leave colours unchanged (see the colour-of-objects entry). Two plane mirrors set at an angle θ produce 360/θ−1 images (three at θ=90°, five at 60°), which is how a kaleidoscope multiplies its chips into symmetric patterns. Two mutually perpendicular mirrors have a very useful property: the outgoing ray is always parallel to the incoming one, merely reversed. Three mirrors pairwise perpendicular—a corner reflector—go further and return light along its own path from any direction. Bicycle tail lights, the micro-prism film in road signs and reflective clothing, corner reflectors on satellites, and the arrays the Apollo missions left on the Moon (still used for laser ranging) are all this; radar and sonar targets carry them too. Periscopes and beam turns may use plane mirrors or total-reflection prisms, the latter needing no coating and lasting better (see the total internal reflection entry). Finally, reflection links to polarization: at about 56° for glass (Brewster's angle) the reflected part is partially polarized, which is why polarized sunglasses can suppress glare from roads and water (see the polarization entry).

oneLiner: 成等大、正立、左右相反的虚像，物像关于镜面对称。
oneLinerEn: Forms an equal, upright, laterally inverted virtual image, symmetric about the mirror.
detail: 平面镜成正立、等大的虚像，像与物关于镜面对称：二者的连线垂直镜面，像到镜面的距离等于物到镜面的距离。所谓虚像，是反射光线反向延长线的交点，不是实际光线会聚之处，因此光屏接不住——这条判据同样适用于所有镜子与透镜的实像／虚像之分，也是本模块一切作图题的入口。常被背诵的「左右相反」其实不准确：镜子交换的是沿法线方向的前后，并不真的分左右；人站着时前后颠倒被大脑读成左右互换，若仰面躺着照镜，颠倒就跑到了上下方向。平面镜成像的实验口径要注意三处：用透明玻璃板代替平面镜，是为了能在镜前看到像同时看到板后的蜡烛，从而定出像的位置；玻璃板必须竖直，否则像与桌面蜡烛错开；比较像与物大小用「等效替代」——拿一支完全相同的蜡烛在板后移动到与像重合（此法与曹冲称象同属替代思想，见「等效替代法」条）。两个高频易错：其一，人走近镜子时像的大小不变，始终与人等高，只是视角变大让人觉得「像更大更清楚」，镜子尺寸不改变像的比例，而能照到全身只需身高一半高的镜子，由两条边缘光线作图即得；其二，水中的「倒影」是平面镜成像（水平镜面使上下颠倒），与「影子」完全是两件事，一个是像、一个是光被遮挡后照不到的区域。面镜家族还有两位：凸面镜发散光束、总是成正立缩小的虚像，却把视野撑大，故汽车后视镜与路口反光镜用它，并配上「镜中物体比看上去更近」的警告语；凹面镜会聚光束，物距足够远时成倒立实像，可作太阳灶、手电筒与车灯的反光碗，剃须镜则利用人靠近焦点后成放大虚像。哈哈镜就是曲率不规则的这两种面镜。潜望镜与穿衣镜属于平面镜成像的应用，而万花筒与光路转向属于反射定律的应用（见「光的反射」条）。
detailEn: A plane mirror forms an upright virtual image exactly the size of the object, with object and image symmetric about the mirror surface: the line joining them is perpendicular to the surface and the image distance equals the object distance. A virtual image is where the backward extensions of the reflected rays meet, not where rays actually converge, so no screen can catch it—the same criterion separates real from virtual images for every mirror and lens in this module and opens every construction problem. The familiar 'left–right reversal' is loose speech: a mirror swaps front and back along its normal, not left and right. Standing upright we read that as a sideways flip; lie on your back in front of the mirror and the reversal moves to the vertical. Three laboratory points matter: a clear glass plate replaces a mirror so you can see both the image and the candle behind the plate and thus locate the image; the plate must stand perfectly vertical or the image will drift off the desk candle; and comparing sizes uses equivalent substitution—move an identical candle until it coincides with the image (the same reasoning as Cao Chong weighing the elephant, see the equivalent-substitution entry). Two frequent errors. First, walking toward a mirror does not enlarge you: the image stays exactly your height, and a larger viewing angle only makes it look bigger (a mirror half your height already shows your whole body, straight from two edge rays). Second, a reflection in water is plane-mirror imaging with a horizontal surface, which flips things top-to-bottom, and has nothing to do with a shadow—one is an image, the other a region light cannot reach. The curved members of the family: a convex mirror diverges the beam and always gives an upright, diminished virtual image while widening the field, hence rear-view mirrors and corner traffic mirrors, complete with the warning that objects are closer than they appear; a concave mirror converges, forms an inverted real image when the object is far off—solar cookers, torch and headlamp reflectors—and shows an enlarged virtual image once you move inside its focus, which is the shaving mirror. Funhouse mirrors are simply these two with irregular curvature. Periscopes and dressing mirrors apply plane-mirror imaging, while kaleidoscopes and beam turning apply the law of reflection (see the reflection entry).

oneLiner: 光斜射入不同介质时传播方向偏折，池中视深变浅。
oneLinerEn: Light bends crossing media obliquely; a pool looks shallower.
detail: 光斜射到两种介质的界面时会同时发生反射与折射，折射定律有两句：折射光线与入射光线、法线共面且分居两侧；n₁sinθ₁=n₂sinθ₂。折射率定义为 n=c/v，真空中恒为 1，空气约 1.0003，水约 1.33，普通玻璃约 1.5，钻石约 2.42，因此光在水里约 22.6 万公里每秒、玻璃里约 20 万公里每秒。由定律立刻得到方向口诀：从光疏进入光密（n 小的进到 n 大的）时折射角小于入射角，光线偏向法线，反之偏离线；正入射时方向不变，只变速度与波长。这里有个必须钉住的分工：折射时频率不变，波速与波长同步变小（v=fλ，频率由光源决定），所以颜色由频率定而不是由波长定。生活中的折射几乎都是视深问题：从岸上看水里的鱼，看到的鱼比真的浅（近似 h′=h/n），叉鱼要瞄准看到的下方；反之从水下看岸上的物体，看到的比真的更高，潜水员头顶的世界被压成一个约 97.6° 的圆窗（其边界正是全反射的临界角，见下条）；插进水里的筷子看起来在水面处折断，玻璃砖后的字被平移，都是同一件事。海市蜃楼则是连续折射：近地面空气热而稀、上层冷而密，光一路弯向密度大的一侧，远处景物的像被抬到空中（上现蜃景常见于海面与雪原，下现蜃景常见于沙漠与柏油路面）；大气折射让日出提前、日落推迟几分钟，也让太阳盘面略扁。历史上惠更斯 1678 年以子波原理推出折射定律，把「光走哪条路」变成「波面上每点都是新波源」的作图法，这是波动说的第一次胜利（见「惠更斯原理」条）。测量口径也要记：中学用插针法或玻璃砖画光路测 n，量的是角度而不是距离，公式的易错点是角必须对法线量。式中 n 为折射率，c 为真空光速，v 为光在该介质中的速度，θ₁、θ₂ 为入射角与折射角，h 与 h′ 为实际深度与看起来的深度。
detailEn: When light strikes an interface obliquely it is both reflected and refracted. The law of refraction has two parts: the refracted ray, the incident ray and the normal lie in one plane on opposite sides of it; and n₁sinθ₁=n₂sinθ₂. The refractive index is n=c/v: exactly 1 in vacuum, about 1.0003 in air, 1.33 in water, 1.5 in ordinary glass, 2.42 in diamond, so light runs at roughly 226,000 km/s in water and 200,000 km/s in glass. The direction rule follows at once—passing from an optically thinner into a denser medium (small n into large n) the refraction angle is smaller than the incidence angle and the ray bends toward the normal, and the other way round; at normal incidence the direction is unchanged and only speed and wavelength alter. A division that must be nailed down: refraction leaves the frequency untouched, while speed and wavelength shrink together (v=fλ, with f fixed by the source), so colour is set by frequency, not wavelength. Almost every everyday example is an apparent-depth problem: fish seen from the bank appear shallower than they are (roughly h′=h/n), so spearing means aiming below the image; seen from under water, objects above the surface stand higher, and a diver looks up into a world compressed into a circular window about 97.6° wide—its rim is exactly the critical angle, see the next entry. A chopstick seems broken at the surface, letters shift sideways under a glass slab, all the same effect. Mirages are continuous refraction: hot thin air at ground level under cold dense air bends light progressively toward the denser side, lifting distant scenery into the sky (superior mirages over sea and snow, inferior ones over deserts and asphalt). Atmospheric refraction brings sunrise forward and delays sunset by several minutes and slightly flattens the solar disk. Historically Huygens derived the law in 1678 from his wavelet principle, turning 'which path does light take' into 'every point of a wavefront is a new source', the first victory of the wave theory (see the Huygens-principle entry). For the lab: pin sighting or a glass slab measures n through angles, not distances, and the trap is that angles are always measured from the normal. In the formulas, n is refractive index, c the vacuum speed of light, v the speed in the medium, θ₁ and θ₂ the angles of incidence and refraction, h the true depth and h′ the apparent depth.

oneLiner: 光从光密到光疏且入射角大于临界角时，全部反射无折射。
oneLinerEn: From dense to rare medium beyond the critical angle, all light reflects.
detail: 全反射有两个门槛，缺一不可：光必须从光密介质射向光疏介质（n 大的一侧出来），且入射角不小于临界角 C。临界角由折射定律在折射角等于 90° 时给出，sinC=1/n（另一侧为空气时）。数值记住三个：水 48.8°、普通玻璃 41.8°、钻石 24.4°。入射角一旦跨过 C，折射光消失，能量几乎全部退回原介质——不是「折射很弱」而是「没有折射」，所以反射率接近 100%，比任何镀银镜面都干净。日常证据很多：水中气泡边缘特别亮、被水浸湿的砂与抛光面看起来发白、从水下往上看水面像一面镜子、潜水员的天空只剩一个约 97.6° 的圆窗，下现蜃景里也有一段是全反射造成的。光学仪器有两个直接受益者：其一，全反射棱镜（等腰直角棱镜）用 45° 入射角轻松越过 41.8° 的临界角，把光转向 90° 或 180°，不用镀层、不怕氧化、寿命长于平面镜，故双筒望远镜与潜望镜多用它；其二，光导纤维把这两条门槛做成结构——内芯 n 略大、包层 n 略小，只要光入射到端面后在内壁的入射角始终大于 C，即使光纤弯曲也能一路全反射传下去；弯曲半径太小、端面不洁或包层被油水印污，都会让一部分光漏出去，这就是「水流导光」演示里水柱能导光而断流就灭的原因。通信光纤的工作窗口约 1.55 μm，优质光纤损耗已低至每公里 0.2 dB 量级；1966 年高锟提出以超纯玻璃做纤维通信的设想并据此获 2009 年诺贝尔物理学奖；医用内窥镜（胃镜）与工业端视镜是同一原理的另一支，短距离照明与传感则用塑料光纤。钻石是这套口径的受益者：n=2.42 使 C 只有 24.4°，加之色散强，好的切工把冠部与亭部的角度算准，让进入的光在内部来回全反射数次后集中从台面射出，形成所谓火彩；切工过浅时光从底部漏走，钻石就显得发黑。最后两处易错：一是「光疏到光密」永远不会全反射，无论角多大；二是临界角随两侧介质与光的颜色而变（n 依赖波长，见「光的色散」条），所以同一界面下紫光先消失、红光后消失。式中 n 为内芯相对外部的折射率之比，C 为临界角。
detailEn: Total internal reflection has two gates, both mandatory: light must travel from the denser medium toward the thinner one (out of the larger n), and the incidence angle must reach or exceed the critical angle C, which comes straight from Snell's law by setting the refraction angle to 90°: sinC=1/n when the outside is air. Memorise three numbers—48.8° for water, 41.8° for ordinary glass, 24.4° for diamond. Once the critical angle is crossed the refracted ray vanishes and essentially all the energy returns to the original medium; this is not 'weak refraction' but 'no refraction', so the reflectance is near unity and cleaner than any silvered mirror. Everyday evidence is plentiful: bubble rims shine under water, wet sand and polished surfaces look pale, the surface acts as a mirror when seen from below, a diver's sky shrinks to a circular window about 97.6° across, and the inferior mirage contains a total-reflection leg. Two instruments profit directly. First, the reflecting prism (an isosceles right-angle block) turns light by 90° or 180° because 45° comfortably exceeds 41.8°; it needs no coating and cannot tarnish, so binoculars and periscopes prefer it to mirrors. Second, the optical fibre builds those two gates into a structure: a core of slightly higher index inside cladding of slightly lower index, so that once light enters the end face at an angle that keeps every internal hit above C, it can walk around bends by total reflection alone. Bend the fibre too tightly, dirty the end face, or let oil and water soak the cladding, and light leaks out—that is why the 'water column light pipe' demo guides light while the falling stream does not. Telecom fibres work near 1.55 μm and the best now lose around 0.2 dB per kilometre; Charles Kao proposed ultra-pure glass fibre communication in 1966 and shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics for it, medical endoscopes and industrial borescopes are the other branch of the same idea, and short-haul lighting and sensing use plastic fibre. Diamond is a beneficiary of this book of numbers: with n=2.42 the critical angle is only 24.4°, and combined with strong dispersion a good cut fixes the crown and pavilion angles so that entering light bounces repeatedly inside and leaves through the table, the so-called fire; cut too shallow and light escapes through the bottom and the stone looks dead. Two last traps: light going from thin to dense never totally reflects, whatever the angle; and the critical angle depends on both media and on colour, since n varies with wavelength (see the dispersion entry), so violet disappears first and red last at the same interface. In the formula, n is the index ratio of core to outside and C is the critical angle.

oneLiner: 凸透镜对光有会聚作用；成像规律由物距 u 决定。
oneLinerEn: Convex lenses converge light; image follows object distance u.
detail: 透镜的分工先讲清：凸透镜把平行光束会聚到焦点，凹透镜把光束发散，看似从另一侧的虚焦点发出。但「会聚／发散」说的是折射后相对于原来的光束更靠轴还是更离轴，不是像的大小，也不是介质的正负——把一块凸透镜放进折射率比它更高的液体里，它会变成发散透镜，这是本条最狠的一处易错。三条特殊光线足以作一切图：平行主轴的光过焦点；过光心的光不偏折；过焦点的光出射后平行主轴。焦距粗测就是让太阳光（近似平行光）在屏上会成最小最亮的光斑，斑到透镜的距离即 f，这也是凸透镜能点火的原因。成像规律按物距 u 逐档而定：u>2f 成倒立缩小实像，像距在 f 与 2f 之间，照相机与眼睛就是这个档位；u=2f 成倒立等大实像，v=2f，此时物与像之间距离最小为 4f；f<u<2f 成倒立放大实像，v>2f，投影仪、幻灯机与手机的近拍都属此档；u=f 不成像，出射平行光（探照灯正是要把灯丝放在焦点上）；u<f 成正立放大虚像，物像同侧，放大镜即此。成实像时的口诀是「物近像远像变大」，而实像都能成在光屏上、虚像不能，这是唯一的判据。实验里三条纪律：烛焰、透镜、光屏三者中心调到同一高度（同轴），否则像跑出台面；光屏上找不到像通常有三种原因——u<f 成的是虚像、u 太接近 f 像远到接不住、或者三心不同高；改用 F 形发光二极管光源比蜡烛更稳且便于比较倒正。透镜的折光本领用焦度表示，D=1/f（f 取米），单位是屈光度，眼镜的「度数」就是它乘 100：+2.00 D 的凸透镜 f=50 cm，−3.00 D 的近视镜 f=−33 cm（见「眼睛与视力矫正」条）。放大镜的放大率约 M=25/f（f 取厘米，25 cm 是明视距离），f=5 cm 即约 5 倍；想再大就撞上衍射极限，须改显微镜（见「显微镜与望远镜」条）。凹透镜另有一用：与凸透镜组合可消色差与消球差，照相机与显微镜的物镜都是多片胶合的透镜组而非单片。式中 u 为物距，v 为像距，f 为焦距，D 为焦度，M 为放大率。
detailEn: Settle the roles first: a convex lens brings a parallel beam to a focus, a concave lens spreads it as if coming from a virtual focus behind it. But converging and diverging mean 'closer to or further from the axis than the incoming bundle', not the size of the image and not the sign of the medium—plunge a convex lens into a liquid of higher refractive index and it turns diverging, the cruellest trap here. Three special rays support every drawing: a ray parallel to the axis leaves through the focus; a ray through the optical centre goes straight; a ray through the focus emerges parallel. Rough focal length measurement just uses sunlight as an almost parallel beam and finds the smallest, brightest patch on a screen—that distance is f, which is also why a convex lens can start a fire. Imaging follows the object distance u in bands: u>2f gives an inverted diminished real image with image distance between f and 2f, the setting of cameras and of the eye; u=2f gives an inverted equal-size real image at v=2f, and here the object-image separation reaches its minimum of 4f; f<u<2f gives an inverted magnified real image with v>2f, the projector, slide lamp and close-focus phone camera; u=f gives no image at all, only a parallel exit beam (which is why a searchlight puts its filament at the focus); u<f gives an upright magnified virtual image on the same side, the magnifying glass. For real images the rule is 'object nearer, image farther and bigger', and the one true test of real versus virtual is whether a screen can catch it. Three laboratory disciplines: align flame, lens and screen centres to one height or the image walks off the paper; failure to find an image has three usual causes—the object is inside f so the image is virtual, u is so close to f that the image is unreachable, or the three centres are not aligned; an F-shaped light-emitting diode source beats a candle for steadiness and for judging inversion. A lens's bending power is its optical power D=1/f with f in metres, the dioptre, and spectacle 'power' is that times 100: a +2.00 D convex lens has f=50 cm, a −3.00 D myopia lens f=−33 cm (see the eye-and-vision entry). A simple magnifier gives about M=25/f with f in centimetres, since 25 cm is the distance of distinct vision, so f=5 cm means roughly ×5; push beyond that and diffraction forbids it, which is the microscope's job (see the microscope-and-telescope entry). Concave lenses have a second use: paired with convex ones they cancel chromatic and spherical aberration, so camera and microscope objectives are cemented multi-element groups, never single glasses. In the formulas, u is object distance, v image distance, f focal length, D optical power and M magnification.

oneLiner: 白光经棱镜分解为七色光，因各色光折射率不同。
oneLinerEn: A prism splits white light into colors because refractive index varies with color.
detail: 白光是复合光，经三棱镜后展开成红橙黄绿蓝靛紫的连续光谱，原因是折射率随波长变化：同一种玻璃对红光的 n 最小、对紫光的 n 最大，于是紫光每一跳都偏得更狠，出射时按颜色被分开——因果链是「n 依赖波长，故偏折角不同」，而不是棱镜「制造」了颜色。牛顿 1666 年的关键实验有两步：先用棱镜把白光展开，再用第二个棱镜把这些色光重新会聚回一束白光，这才排除了「是棱镜把光染了色」的另一种解释，这一步反向复合常被教科书略去。彩虹是同一条链在水滴里完成：阳光进入水滴折射一次、在底面反射一次、再折射出来，主虹的红光出射方向与入射阳光夹角约 42°、紫光约 40°，因此背对太阳时红在外圈紫在内圈；霓是水滴内反射两次的结果，夹角约 51°、颜色顺序反转且更暗。看彩虹的条件是空气里有大量水滴而太阳在身后低处，故雨后傍晚最常见，背着太阳喷一片水雾也能造出小彩虹。天空蓝与夕阳红既不是折射也不是色散而是散射：空气分子对光的散射强度约与波长的四次方成反比（瑞利散射），蓝光被散得最厉害，于是整个天空都发蓝；日落时阳光要穿过比正午厚得多的气层，蓝光沿途被剥掉，剩下的偏红橙；云与雾的滴子大得多，属几乎不挑波长的米氏散射，所以呈白与灰。不可见光谱的两端也归这一条管：红光之外是红外线，1800 年赫歇尔把温度计拖到光谱红端之外，发现那里升温最快，红外主要体现为热作用，遥控器、热像仪与夜视仪靠它；紫光之外是紫外线，1801 年里特靠氯化银变黑找到它，紫外化学作用强，能杀菌（波长约 254 nm 最有效）、能让荧光物质发光，故验钞与防伪用它，也正是它把皮肤晒伤。色散在仪器上通常是要克服的毛病：单片透镜对不同色光焦距不同，像边缘带彩（色差），18 世纪用冕牌与火石两种玻璃胶合成消色差透镜才压住；而棱镜与光栅则把色散做成工具，光谱仪的核心就是它——太阳光谱里那些暗的夫琅禾费线，正是本生与基尔霍夫把谱线对应到元素、进而读出恒星成分的依据（见「能级与氢原子光谱」条）。光纤里不同颜色的光跑得不一样快也会拖累带宽，这叫色散，是长途通信必须补偿的问题（见「全反射」条）。颜料与色光的混合规矩不同，见「色光的三原色」条。
detailEn: White light is a mixture: a prism spreads it into the continuous band red-orange-yellow-green-blue-violet because refractive index depends on wavelength—same glass, smallest n for red, largest for violet, so violet bends harder at every refraction and the colours pull apart. The chain of causation is 'n varies with wavelength, therefore the deviation differs', never 'the prism invented the colours'. Newton's crucial experiment of 1666 had two steps: spread white light with a prism, then recombine the colours with a second prism back into white, which is what ruled out the rival explanation that the glass was dyeing the light; this recombination half is often left out of textbooks. A rainbow is the same chain inside droplets: light refracts on entering a drop, reflects once off its back wall and refracts out again, with red leaving about 42° from the incoming sunlight and violet about 40°, so with the Sun behind you red sits on the outer edge; the secondary bow comes from two internal reflections, sits near 51°, reverses the order and is dimmer. You need abundant droplets in the air and a low Sun behind your back—hence rainbows after evening showers, and a spray bottle facing away from the Sun makes a small one. Blue sky and red sunsets are neither refraction nor dispersion but scattering: molecular scattering goes roughly as the inverse fourth power of wavelength (Rayleigh), so blue is flung around most vigorously and fills the whole sky; at sunset the light crosses a far thicker slab of atmosphere and the blue is stripped off along the way, leaving red and orange; cloud and fog droplets are much larger and scatter almost wavelength-blind (Mie), which is why they look white or grey. The two ends beyond the visible belong here too: infrared was found in 1800 by Herschel, who dragged a thermometer past the red end of the spectrum and saw the fastest rise there, and its signature is heat—remotes, thermal cameras and night-vision devices use it; ultraviolet was found in 1801 by Ritter through silver chloride darkening, acts strongly in chemistry, kills microbes (most effective near 254 nm) and makes fluorescent materials glow, which is what banknote and anti-counterfeit checks exploit—and what sunburns skin. In instruments dispersion is usually a defect to be beaten: a single lens has different focal lengths for different colours, ringing images with colour, and only the 18th-century achromatic doublet of crown and flint glass tamed it; prisms and gratings, conversely, turn dispersion into the working part of a spectroscope—the dark Fraunhofer lines across the solar spectrum are what let Bunsen and Kirchhoff map lines onto elements and eventually read the composition of stars (see the hydrogen-spectrum entry). In optical fibre, colours travelling at different speeds also throttle the link, again called dispersion, and must be compensated for in long hauls (see the total internal reflection entry). Pigments mix by different rules, covered in the additive-primaries entry.

oneLiner: 两列相干光叠加成明暗条纹（干涉）；光绕过障碍偏离直线（衍射）。
oneLinerEn: Coherent light adds to bright/dark fringes (interference); light bends around obstacles (diffraction).
detail: 干涉与衍射是波独有的签名，正是它们把光从「粒子流」判给「波」。干涉的条件是相干：两列光频率相同且相位差恒定；两盏普通灯永不相干，因为原子发光的波列是随机的。杨氏因此在 1801—1803 年用同一束光经过双缝分成两路来保证相干。判据看路程差：路程差等于波长整数倍处加强、半波长奇数倍处减弱，屏上相邻明纹间距 Δx=λL/d——取缝距 d=0.2 mm、缝到屏 L=1 m、波长 λ=600 nm，算得 3 mm，条纹清晰可数，这正是实验室做得出的量级。用白光做双缝时中央是白色亮纹、两侧出现彩色带，因为各色条纹间距不同。薄膜干涉是同一原理的另一实现：光在薄膜上下两个表面各反射一次后相干，肥皂泡与油膜的彩色来自膜厚与波长可比；增透膜把厚度做到约 λ/(4n)，让两束反射光相消、透射光增强，相机镜头与镀膜眼镜上那点蓝紫反光就是它的签名；检查平台平不平用「牛顿环」，条纹弯在哪里，工件就凹在哪里。衍射是光绕过障碍偏离直线，一切波都衍射，但明显与否取决于障碍或孔的尺寸与波长是否相当：声波的波长从厘米到十几米，所以隔墙「闻其声而不见其人」办得到；可见光只有 400—700 nm，故日常只见直线传播，须用狭缝、细丝或小针孔才看得出。圆孔与圆板的衍射会在几何阴影的正中留下一个亮斑：1818 年法国科学院的征文竞赛中，泊松从菲涅耳的波动理论推出这个他自认荒谬的结论意在反驳，阿拉果随即真的测到它，史称泊松亮斑——一次旨在推翻理论的预言反倒成了理论最漂亮的证据。激光出现后相干不再稀缺，全息术因此可行：记录物光与参考光的干涉图样等于同时保存了振幅与相位，故能重建出立体的像（伽博 1947 年提出这一想法，并获 1971 年诺贝尔物理学奖）。衍射同时设下分辨的天花板：仪器最小可分辨角约 1.22λ/D，口径越大看得越细；显微镜最小分辨距离约 0.61λ/NA，取 550 nm 与最高数值孔径 1.4 得约 0.24 μm，这就是光学显微镜放大到约 1600 倍便再无信息可挖、须改用电子显微镜的原因（见「显微镜与望远镜」条）。式中 λ 为波长，d 为双缝间距，L 为缝到屏的距离，Δx 为相邻亮纹间距，D 为口径，NA 为数值孔径。
detailEn: Interference and diffraction are the exclusive signatures of waves, and it was these that moved light off the particle ledger and onto the wave one. Interference demands coherence: equal frequency and a steady phase difference. Two ordinary lamps can never interfere, since atoms emit in random wave-trains, which is why Young in 1801–1803 split one beam through two slits to guarantee it. The test is path difference: constructive where it is a whole number of wavelengths, destructive at odd half-wavelengths, and the spacing of bright fringes on the screen is Δx=λL/d—take slit separation d=0.2 mm, screen distance L=1 m and wavelength λ=600 nm and you get 3 mm, an easy pattern to count in the lab. With white light the central fringe is white and the flanks are coloured, because each colour spaces its fringes differently. Thin-film interference is the same principle in another guise: two reflections off the two faces of a film interfere, and soap bubbles and oil slicks colour because film thickness is comparable to wavelength; an anti-reflection coating is made about λ/(4n) thick so the two reflected beams cancel and transmission rises—the faint blue-purple sheen on camera lenses and coated spectacles is its signature; testing optical flatness with 'Newton's rings' reads a bump or dip straight off the bent fringe. Diffraction is light bending round obstacles; every wave does it, and whether it is obvious depends on whether obstacle or aperture size is comparable to the wavelength: sound runs from centimetres to tens of metres, so you can hear round a wall without seeing the speaker, while visible light at 400–700 nm demands a narrow slit, a hair or a pinhole before anything shows. Circular apertures and discs throw a bright spot into the middle of the geometric shadow: in the 1818 French Academy prize contest Poisson derived that absurd-looking consequence from Fresnel's wave theory expecting to refute it, and Arago promptly observed it—Poisson's bright spot, an attempted kill-shot that became the theory's finest evidence. Once lasers made coherence cheap, holography followed: recording the interference of object and reference beams stores phase as well as amplitude, so a three-dimensional image can be rebuilt (Gabor conceived this in 1947 and took the 1971 Nobel Prize). Diffraction also caps resolution: the smallest separable angle is about 1.22λ/D, so bigger apertures see finer, and a light microscope cannot resolve below roughly 0.61λ/NA—about 0.24 μm at 550 nm with the best oil-immersion objective—which is why magnifying past some 1600× buys nothing and electron microscopes take over (see the microscope-and-telescope entry). In the formulas, λ is wavelength, d slit separation, L slit-to-screen distance, Δx fringe spacing, D aperture and NA numerical aperture.

oneLiner: 横波特有的振动方向选择性，证明光是横波。
oneLinerEn: Directional filtering of vibration, proving light is transverse.
detail: 偏振讲的是振动方向的选择性，因此它是横波独有的性质：只有振动方向与传播方向垂直的波，才谈得上「只放行某个方向」。自然光（太阳、灯丝）在垂直于传播的平面内各方向均匀，通过一片偏振片后只留一个分量，强度约减半；再把第二片转到与第一片正交，光就完全过不去、屏全黑——这个「双偏振片消光」是光是横波最直接的一条证据，与电磁波里 E 与 B 相互垂直且都垂直于传播方向的口径接得上（见「交变电流与电磁波」条）。定量关系是马吕斯定律 I=I₀cos²θ；马吕斯 1808 年发现光的偏振，而偏振被安到横波的位置上则要靠后来的电磁理论。日常里偏振处处在：水面、玻璃与路面反射的光是部分偏振的，掠射时最明显，玻璃在约 56°（布鲁斯特角，tanθ=n₂/n₁）附近反射的光几乎完全线偏振，偏振太阳镜正是挡掉这一方向，于是开车与钓鱼时既压掉刺眼反光又不至于把整个视野调暗一半。看立体电影时，影院用两台放映机以互相垂直的偏振方向把左右眼画面叠在同一块银幕上，眼镜不过是两片方向不同的偏振片；液晶显示本身不发光，靠液晶分子旋转偏振方向、再由偏振片决定亮暗，因此戴着偏振镜看手机屏幕会莫名发黑，反过来两片偏振片也能验出一块屏是不是液晶。透明塑料受力时显出彩色条纹，这是光弹效应，工程上用它给桥梁与齿轮模型的应力分布拍照；糖溶液能使偏振面旋转，旋光仪据此测浓度，制糖与制药车间常年使用；天空的散射光部分偏振，偏振摄影滤镜压在镜头上可以把蓝天压暗、白云更跳，蜜蜂一类昆虫也靠天空的偏振模式在阴天里导航。反过来，空气中的声波是纵波，无论叠多少片「偏振片」都不会消光，这本身就是横波与纵波最好的一组对照（见「声音的产生与传播」条）。光纤里两个偏振方向的速度略有差别，会产生偏振模色散，是高速通信要处理的问题之一。式中 I 为透射光强，I₀ 为自然光过第一片后的光强，θ 为两片偏振片透振方向的夹角，n₁、n₂ 为界面两侧介质的折射率。
detailEn: Polarization is about a preference of vibration direction, so it belongs to transverse waves alone: only a wave whose vibration is perpendicular to its travel can be said to pass just one direction. Natural light (Sun, filament) is uniform in the plane transverse to propagation, so one polarizer leaves about half the intensity; cross a second polarizer at 90° and the screen goes black. That extinction between crossed polarizers is the most direct evidence that light is transverse, and it lines up with the statement that in an electromagnetic wave E and B are mutually perpendicular and both perpendicular to the direction of travel (see the em-waves entry). The quantitative rule is Malus's law, I=I₀cos²θ; Malus discovered the polarization of light in 1808, while placing polarization inside the transverse-wave picture took the later electromagnetic theory. Polarization is everywhere in daily life: light reflected from water, glass and roadways is partially polarized, most strongly at grazing incidence, and near 56° for glass (Brewster's angle, tanθ=n₂/n₁) the reflected light is almost fully linearly polarized—polarized sunglasses simply block that direction, cutting glare on the road or while fishing without dimming the whole view by half. Stereoscopic films work by two projectors laying left- and right-eye pictures on one screen at crossed polarizations, and the glasses are nothing but two differently oriented polarizing sheets. LCDs emit no light: liquid crystal rotates the polarization and a polarizer then decides bright or dark, which is why a phone screen goes black when viewed through a polarizer, and why two sheets can test whether a screen is a liquid-crystal display. Stressed transparent plastic shows coloured fringes—the photoelastic effect, used to photograph stress distributions in bridge and gear models; sugar solutions rotate the polarization plane, which the polarimeter turns into a concentration reading, a routine in sugar and pharmaceutical plants; scattered skylight is partially polarized, so a polarizing camera filter darkens the sky and lifts the clouds, and insects such as bees navigate on overcast days by that polarization pattern. Sound in air, by contrast, is longitudinal: stack as many 'polarizers' as you like and it never extinguishes, which is itself the cleanest transverse-versus-longitudinal contrast (see the sound-propagation entry). In fibre optics the two polarization directions travel at slightly different speeds, giving polarization-mode dispersion, one of the problems high-speed links must handle. In the formulas, I is transmitted intensity, I₀ the intensity after the first sheet, θ the angle between the two transmission axes, and n₁, n₂ the refractive indices either side of the interface.

oneLiner: 晶状体把像成在视网膜上，近视用凹透镜、远视用凸透镜矫正。
oneLinerEn: The lens focuses images on the retina; myopia is fixed with a diverging lens, hyperopia with a converging one.
detail: 眼睛是一架会自调焦的照相机：角膜与晶状体共同折光（角膜其实贡献了大部分折光力），在视网膜上成一个倒立、缩小的实像，感光细胞把光信号交给视神经，而「正立的世界」是大脑翻读之后的结果——所以「眼睛里成的是倒像」与「我们看见的是正立的」两句同时成立，把它们当成矛盾是常见错误。瞳孔是光阑，强光下缩小、弱光下放大（暗处可扩到约 8 mm）；看近物时睫状肌收缩、晶状体变凸、折光力增强，这叫调节，看远时相反。正常眼能看清的最近点叫近点，青少年约 10 cm 且随年龄推远；长时间阅读最舒适的距离约 25 cm，称明视距离，放大镜的放大率正是以它为基准（见「透镜与凸透镜成像」条）。近视的原因是眼球前后轴过长或晶状体折光过强，远物的像成在视网膜之前，故看远模糊、看近反而清楚，矫正要戴凹透镜让光先发散一些；远视则是像倾向于成在视网膜之后，看远看近都得动用调节，配凸透镜。老花与远视不是一回事：它是晶状体随年龄变硬、调节能力下降、近点后移，看小字要拿远，凸透镜只是代偿那份失去的调节，所以「年轻人近视、老年人老花」两套口径不能混。配镜的度数用焦度表示，D=1/f（f 取米），−3.00 D 即焦距约 −33 cm 的凹透镜，+2.00 D 即 f=50 cm 的凸透镜；散光是角膜在不同子午线方向上不平，各方向折光力不一，须用柱面透镜。保护视力第一位的是姿势、光照与时间分配：常见建议是连续用眼二三十分钟后抬头看远几十秒，让调节肌松弛，每天足够的户外活动对抑制近视加深有帮助；耳机则要限音量限时长按（见「噪声的危害与控制」条）。两个补充口径：视网膜上视神经穿出的地方没有感光细胞，像落在那里就看不见，这叫盲点，因两眼视野互补且大脑会填补而平时察觉不到；眯眼或在小孔后看远处会更清楚，因为挡住了边缘乱折的光、只让近轴光进入，与「光的直线传播」条里的小孔成像同源。式中 D 为焦度（屈光度），f 为透镜焦距（以米计，凹透镜取负）。
detailEn: The eye is a self-focusing camera: cornea and lens bend the light together (the cornea in fact supplies most of the power) and form an inverted, diminished real image on the retina, whose cells hand the signal to the optic nerve, while the upright world is what the brain reads out afterwards—so 'the eye images upside down' and 'we see things upright' are both true at once, and treating them as a contradiction is a standard error. The pupil is the aperture, constricting in bright light and dilating in the dark (to some 8 mm); for near work the ciliary muscle contracts, the lens bulges and its power rises, which is called accommodation, and the reverse happens at distance. The nearest point a normal eye can focus is the near point, roughly 10 cm in the young and receding with age; the comfortable sustained viewing distance is about 25 cm, the distance of distinct vision, which is the baseline for a magnifier's power (see the lens-imaging entry). Myopia comes from an eyeball that is too long or a lens system that is too strong, so distant objects focus in front of the retina—far looks blurred while near stays sharp—and it is corrected by a diverging lens that spreads the light first. Hyperopia focuses behind the retina and must spend accommodation on far and near alike, so a converging lens is prescribed. Presbyopia is not hyperopia: the lens hardens with age, accommodation fails and the near point retreats, so small print gets held away, and the converging lens merely stands in for the lost accommodation—'young people short-sighted, old people long-sighted for reading' are two different accounts and must not be merged. Spectacle power is measured in dioptres, D=1/f with f in metres: −3.00 D is a diverging lens of about −33 cm focal length, +2.00 D a converging lens at 50 cm; astigmatism means the cornea is uneven across meridians, with different power in different directions, needing a cylindrical lens. Vision protection starts with posture, lighting and time management: a common recommendation is to look far away for tens of seconds after every half-hour of close work to release the ciliary muscle, and ample outdoor daylight helps slow myopia progression; earphones need limits on volume and duration (see the noise-control entry). Two side notes: where the optic nerve leaves the retina there are no photoreceptors, so an image there is simply missing—the blind spot goes unnoticed because the two eyes overlap and the brain fills in; and squinting, or viewing through a small hole, sharpens distance vision by blocking the wildly bent marginal rays and admitting only paraxial ones, the same physics as the pinhole in the rectilinear-propagation entry. In the formula, D is optical power in dioptres and f the focal length in metres, taken negative for a diverging lens.

oneLiner: 两组透镜接力放大：显微镜看清近处微小物体，望远镜拉近远处巨大目标。
oneLinerEn: Two lens stages relay magnification: microscopes resolve tiny nearby objects, telescopes bring distant ones close.
detail: 显微镜与望远镜都是两段透镜接力，取向却相反：显微镜要看清近处的微小，望远镜要把远处的巨大拉近，而两者的判据都是视角——眼睛能分辨的最小视角约 1 角分，一切放大装置的本质都是增大进入眼睛的视角，而不是「把像做大」。显微镜把标本放在短焦物镜的一倍与二倍焦距之间，先成一个倒立放大的实像，落进目镜焦点之内，目镜再充当放大镜把这个实像放大成虚像；总放大率是两段乘积 M=m₁×m₂，10×40 即 400 倍。真正的限制不在放大而在分辨：可见光波长 400—700 nm，衍射使最小分辨距离约 0.61λ/NA，最好的油浸物镜也只能到 0.2 μm 上下，于是光学显微镜放大到约 1600 倍再无信息可挖，继续放大只是空放大；要看更小的须改用电子显微镜，因为 100 kV 电子的德布罗意波长仅约 3.7 pm，比光短几万倍（见「波粒二象性」条）。望远镜有两条血统：开普勒式用两只凸透镜，物镜焦距长、目镜焦距短，放大率 M=f物/f目，成倒像，但镜筒内那个实像处可以装十字分划板用于测量，故天文与瞄准具多用它；伽利略式以凹透镜做目镜，成正立像、镜筒短、视场窄，剧院望远镜走这条路线，而 1609 年伽利略把它指向天空，看到了月面环形山、木星的四颗卫星与金星的盈亏。反射式由牛顿 1668 年做出，用抛物面镜取代物镜，一举消掉色差，也才把口径做得大——决定一台望远镜好坏的首要指标是口径而不是倍数：集光力按 D² 增长，角分辨率约 1.22λ/D，10 cm 口径在可见光下约 1.4 角秒，而暗适应的人眼凭约 7 mm 瞳孔只能看到 6 等星，大口径意味着更暗、更细都看得见。当代例子包括 2.4 m 的哈勃空间望远镜与地面 8—10 m 级大望远镜；射电波段的波长要长得多，分辨率只能靠更大的天线面（如 500 m 口径的 FAST）与干涉阵列补回来（见「光年与宇宙尺度」条）。同一台望远镜换更短焦的目镜倍数更高，但像更暗、抖动也更明显，故观测者宁取适中倍率换清晰与稳定。式中 M 为放大率，m₁、m₂ 为物镜与目镜各自的放大倍数，f物、f目 为物镜与目镜焦距，D 为口径，λ 为波长，NA 为数值孔径。
detailEn: Both instruments relay two lens stages but in opposite directions: a microscope must resolve the tiny nearby, a telescope must pull the vast far away, and the yardstick for both is visual angle—the eye separates about one arcminute, so any magnifier works by enlarging the angle subtended at the eye, not by 'making the image big'. A microscope puts the specimen between one and two focal lengths of a short-focus objective, which paints an inverted magnified real image inside the eyepiece's focus; the eyepiece then acts as a simple magnifier on that image. Total magnification is the product M=m₁×m₂, so 10×40 means 400×. The real limit is resolution, not magnification: with visible wavelengths of 400–700 nm, diffraction holds the smallest resolvable spacing near 0.61λ/NA, about 0.2 μm even for the best oil immersion, so past roughly 1600× an optical microscope yields no further information and more magnification is empty; smaller things need an electron microscope, since a 100 kV electron's de Broglie wavelength is only about 3.7 pm, tens of thousands of times shorter (see the wave-particle entry). Telescopes come in two lineages. The Keplerian uses two convex lenses, long-focus objective and short-focus eyepiece, M=f_obj/f_eye, giving an inverted image but leaving a real image inside the tube where a crosshair graticule can sit—hence its use in astronomy and sights. The Galilean uses a concave eyepiece, stays upright, short and narrow-fielded, which is the opera glass; in 1609 Galileo turned one skyward and found cratered mountains on the Moon, four satellites of Jupiter and the phases of Venus. Newton's 1668 reflector replaced the objective with a parabolic mirror, ending chromatic aberration outright and allowing large apertures—and aperture, not magnification, is the primary spec: light gathering grows as D², angular resolution is about 1.22λ/D, so a 10 cm instrument reaches some 1.4 arcseconds in visible light where the dark-adapted eye, with a 7 mm pupil, tops out near sixth magnitude. Flagship examples are the 2.4 m Hubble and ground-based 8–10 m class telescopes; at radio wavelengths, where λ is enormously longer, resolution is recovered only with huge dishes (the 500 m FAST) and interferometer arrays (see the cosmic-distance entry). Swapping to a shorter eyepiece raises magnification but dims and shakes the image, so observers usually trade magnification for steadiness and clarity. In the formulas, M is magnification, m₁ and m₂ the objective and eyepiece contributions, f_obj and f_eye their focal lengths, D the aperture, λ the wavelength and NA the numerical aperture.

oneLiner: 透明物体的颜色由透过它的色光决定，不透明物体由它反射的色光决定。
oneLinerEn: A transparent object's color is set by the light it transmits; an opaque one's by the light it reflects.
detail: 物体的颜色不是它自带的涂料，而是它对照明光谱做了一次筛选：不透明物体的颜色由它反射的色光决定，透明物体的颜色由它透过的色光决定。红纸只反射红光而吸收其余，红玻璃只透过红光而吸收其余；白光下物体显出「本色」，一旦换成单色光源就露底——只有红光的工作灯下，蓝布把光全部吸收而近乎全黑，绿光下的红玫瑰同样发暗，这就是车间、机房与舞台用有色光时颜色不可信的原因。黑色吸收几乎全部可见光因而升温（夏天深色车身与沥青路面烫手，极地用黑冰取火），白色反射几乎全部所以凉爽；沙漠里宽松的长黑袍并不违背这条吸收规律，它靠袍内空气对流把热带走。滤色镜是这套规则的工程用法：在镜头前加一片只放行某段光的玻璃或树脂，黄滤镜吸收蓝光从而压暗蓝天、让白云更跳，是黑白摄影的经典手段，舞台分色、生化检测与荧光显微里的激发块同理（见「光的色散」「偏振」条）。有一类颜色根本不含色素，而是结构造出来的：蝴蝶翅膀、孔雀羽毛与光盘背面的彩虹，来自薄膜干涉与光栅衍射把不同颜色的光分方向弹开，因此随视角变色，也不会因化学作用褪色，这叫结构色（见「干涉与衍射」条）。另一类是先吸收再发出：荧光物质吸收紫外线后立即发出可见光，故验钞、防伪标记与荧光笔在紫外灯下极亮；夜光材料则吸收后缓慢释放，属磷光。「光本身的颜色」与「物体的颜色」要分开，而人最终看到的颜色是三种视锥细胞响应的组合，同一颜色感觉可以由完全不同的光谱产生——这叫作同色异谱，正是屏幕能用三色像素骗过眼睛、而一盏灯的「显色指数」需要单独评价的原因（见「色光的三原色」条）。天体的颜色也走这条路：恒星偏蓝说明表面温度高、偏红说明温度低，红巨星与蓝白星的颜色差就是这么读的（见「恒星的一生」条）。
detailEn: An object's colour is not paint it carries but a filter it applies to the light reaching it: an opaque object's colour is set by the light it reflects, a transparent one's by the light it transmits. Red paper reflects red and absorbs the rest; red glass passes red and absorbs the rest. Under white light things show their 'own' colour, but change the source and the mask slips—under a red-only work lamp blue cloth absorbs everything and goes nearly black, and a red rose under green light is equally dim, which is exactly why colours are untrustworthy under coloured lighting in workshops, machine rooms and stages. Black absorbs almost the whole visible band and heats up (dark car bodies and asphalt burn the hand in summer; black ice was used to start fires in the polar night), white reflects nearly all of it and stays cool; the loose black robe of desert nomads does not defy that absorption law—it sheds heat through the air current inside the robe. Colour filters are the engineered version: put a sheet of glass or resin that passes only part of the spectrum in front of a lens, and a yellow filter soaks up blue, darkening the sky and lifting the clouds, the classic black-and-white trick, with the same logic behind stage gels and the excitation blocks of fluorescence microscopy (see the dispersion and polarization entries). A class of colour contains no pigment at all: butterfly wings, peacock feathers and the rainbow on a compact disc come from thin-film interference and grating diffraction flinging different colours into different directions, so they shift with viewing angle and never fade chemically—structural colour (see the interference-and-diffraction entry). Another class absorbs first and then re-emits: fluorescent materials take in ultraviolet and promptly return visible light, which is why banknote checks, security marks and highlighter ink blaze under a UV lamp, while glow-in-the-dark stores release slowly, which is phosphorescence. Keep 'the colour of light' separate from 'the colour of objects', and remember that the colour you finally see is a combination of three cone responses: identical colour sensations can come from utterly different spectra—metamerism—which is why three-pixel screens can fool the eye, and why a lamp's colour-rendering index has to be graded separately (see the additive-primaries entry). Celestial colours follow the same road: a blue star has a hotter surface than a red one, and that is how red giants and blue-white stars are read apart (see the life-of-stars entry).

oneLiner: 红、绿、蓝三色光按不同比例混合可得各种色光，等量混合即为白光。
oneLinerEn: Red, green and blue light mix in varying ratios to yield all colors; equal parts give white.
detail: 色光的三原色是红、绿、蓝，规矩是加色混合：叠得越多越亮，红加绿得黄、红加蓝得品红、绿加蓝得青，三色等量即白光。这里必须解释「红加绿为什么是黄」：它并没有造出波长 580 nm 的黄光，而是同时刺激了眼里对红与对绿敏感的两种视锥细胞，而一束真正的黄光刺激的正是同一组合，大脑把两种输入读成同一种感觉。这一「同色异谱」的事实是整个色度学的地基，也是屏幕能工作的理由：手机与显示器把红绿蓝子像素排成点阵，靠人眼分辨极限在远处把它们混成一色，逐点调节三种光的强度就铺得出可显示的全部颜色；视频制式与色彩管理里的 sRGB、DCI-P3 等色域概念，说的都是这三条通道能覆盖多大范围。另一套三原色属于颜料与油墨，规矩是减色混合：品红、黄、青，每一种都吞掉一段光谱、把剩下的反射出来，混得越多被吃掉的光越多，所以颜料越调越暗，三色等量趋近黑；实际印刷用青、品红、黄再加一支黑（CMYK），黑色单独上墨，既省掉把三种染料叠成脏黑的代价，也能把暗部压下去。两套原色常被交叉着考，判据只有一条：光源发光走加色，被反射或被透过的颜料与滤色片走减色。几个连带结论：白光能被棱镜分回七色又能重新复合，说明它是复合光（见「光的色散」条）；钠灯发出的是几乎单一波长的黄光，看上去与「红加绿」的黄一样，但光谱完全不同，这是同色异谱最干净的实例；物体的颜色由它反射或透过的那部分决定，与三原色规则相乘而不是相加（见「物体的颜色」条）；红绿色盲者缺某一种视锥细胞，因而对混色识别图失效，这从生理一侧证明了加色混合走的是三条通道而不是无数条。
detailEn: The additive primaries of light are red, green and blue, and the rule is addition: the more you stack, the brighter it gets—red plus green gives yellow, red plus blue gives magenta, green plus blue gives cyan, and all three in equal measure give white. The question 'why does red plus green look yellow' must be answered properly: no 580 nm yellow light has been created; instead the two cones sensitive to red and to green are stimulated together, and a genuinely yellow beam stimulates the very same pair, so the brain reads both inputs as one sensation. This metamerism is the foundation of the whole of colorimetry and the reason screens work: displays pack red, green and blue subpixels into a matrix, let the eye's resolution limit merge them at a distance, and paint every displayable colour by dialling the three intensities point by point; the colour-space names of video and colour management, sRGB and DCI-P3 among them, simply describe how much territory those three channels can cover. The other set of primaries belongs to pigments and ink and works by subtraction: magenta, yellow and cyan, each swallowing a slice of the spectrum and reflecting the rest, so mixing more of them eats more light and paints get darker as you blend, with all three approaching black. Practical printing therefore uses cyan, magenta, yellow plus a separate black (CMYK), the black saving the cost of stacking three dyes into a muddy dark and giving the shadows real depth. Exam questions cross the two sets constantly, and there is one test: a source that emits light follows addition, while reflected or transmitted pigment and filter follow subtraction. Consequences worth carrying: white light can be split into seven colours by a prism and recombined again, proving it composite (see the dispersion entry); a sodium lamp emits almost a single wavelength of yellow that looks identical to 'red plus green' yet has an utterly different spectrum, the cleanest instance of metamerism; an object's colour is decided by the slice it reflects or transmits, which multiplies with rather than adds to the primary rules (see the colour-of-objects entry); and red-green colour blindness, caused by a missing cone type, defeats pseudo-isochromatic plates, proving from the physiological side that additive mixing runs on three channels rather than on countless ones.
